My current finding is that the side‑length conditions force  

\[
a=BC=F_{n+2},\qquad 
b=CA=s-F_n,\qquad 
c=AB=s-F_{n+1},
\]

where the semiperimeter \(s\) can be any real number \(>F_{n+2}\).  Consequently  

\[
BD=s-b=F_n,\qquad CD=s-c=F_{n+1},
\]

so the only free parameter of an \(n\)-tastic triangle is the semiperimeter \(s\) (or equivalently the ratio \(b/c\)).  All other quantities (the incircle radius, the points \(E,F,D,N\), etc.) are determined once \(s\) is chosen.  This reduces the geometric search to a one‑parameter family.

My current finding is that the incircle‑contact conditions only fix the base \(BC\) and the difference \(b-c\):  

\[
BC=F_{n+2},\qquad BD=s-b=F_n,\qquad CD=s-c=F_{n+1},
\]

so that \(b-c=F_{n-1}\).  Hence any triangle with side lengths  

\[
a=F_{n+2},\qquad b=s-F_n,\qquad c=s-F_{n+1}
\]

(and any semiperimeter \(s> \max\{F_n,F_{n+1}\}\)) satisfies the incircle distances.  The extra cyclic condition \(B,K,N,K'\) must therefore impose a single additional relation that fixes the free parameter \(s\) (or equivalently the apex position).

My current finding is that the side‑length conditions force the semiperimeter \(s\) to be a free parameter:  

\[
a=BC=F_{n+2},\qquad b=CA=s-F_n,\qquad c=AB=s-F_{n+1},
\]

with the only restriction \(s>F_{n+2}\). Consequently  

\[
b-c=F_{n-1},\qquad\frac{b}{c}=1+\frac{F_{n-1}}{s-F_{n+1}},
\]

so as \(s\to\infty\) the triangle becomes asymptotically isosceles (\(b/c\to1\)). This shows the family of \(n\)-tastic triangles has a single free scale parameter \(s\).

My current finding is that the side‑length condition “\(BD=F_n,\;CD=F_{n+1}\)” forces  
\[
BD=s-b,\qquad CD=s-c,
\]  
where \(s\) is the semiperimeter of \(\triangle ABC\). Hence for any \(n\) we have the one‑parameter family  
\[
b=s-F_n,\qquad c=s-F_{n+1},\qquad a=BC=F_{n+2},
\]  
with the only restriction \(s>F_{n+2}\) (so that \(b,c>0\) and the triangle inequality holds). Thus the geometry of the problem reduces to a single free variable \(s\) (or equivalently the ratio \(b/c\)), while the Fibonacci data are already built in. This parametrisation will be the basis for imposing the extra cyclic condition \(B,K,N,K'\) and for maximizing \(\dfrac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\).

My current finding is that every \(n\)-tastic triangle is completely described by a single positive parameter  

\[
t:=s-a>0,
\]

where \(a=BC=F_{n+2}\) and \(s\) is the semiperimeter.  In terms of \(t\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
AB&=c=F_n+t,\\
AC&=b=F_{n+1}+t,\\
\text{incircle radius }r&=\sqrt{\frac{t\,F_nF_{n+1}}{F_{n+2}+t}},\\
\text{incircle centre }I&=(F_n,r),\qquad D=(F_n,0).
\end{aligned}
\]

All other points (\(A,F,E,N,K,K'\)) are determined from these data, so the family of \(n\)-tastic triangles has exactly one free degree of freedom (the scale‑parameter \(t\)).  This reduction will allow the remaining constraints (especially the cyclicity of \(K N K' B\)) to be expressed as a single equation in \(t\).

My current finding is that the cyclic condition \(B,K,N,K'\) forces the line \(BN\) to be the internal angle bisector of \(\angle KBK'\). Since \(K'\) is the reflection of \(K\) across \(EF\), the angle \(\angle KBK'\) equals twice the angle between \(BK\) and the line \(EF\); thus the condition is equivalent to \(\angle KBN=\angle N B K'\). Using coordinates \(B=(0,0),\;C=(F_{n+2},0),\;D=(F_n,0),\;I=(F_n,r)\) and the parametrisation \(b=s-F_n,\;c=s-F_{n+1}\) (with \(s>F_{n+2}\)), this yields the explicit equation  

\[
\frac{(s-F_n)^2-(s-F_{n+1})^2}{(s-F_n)(s-F_{n+1})}=2\frac{r}{F_n},
\]

which uniquely determines the semiperimeter \(s\) (hence the triangle shape) for each \(n\). This reduces the problem to a single‑parameter family where \(s\) is fixed by the above relation, allowing the ratio \(\dfrac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\) to be expressed solely in terms of \(n\).

My current finding is that the cyclic condition \(B,K,N,K'\) can be expressed as a single algebraic equation in the single free parameter \(s\) (or equivalently the ratio \(b/c\)).  

Using coordinates \(B=(0,0),C=(a,0),D=(F_n,0),I=(F_n,r)\) with \(a=F_{n+2}\) and \(b=s-F_n,\;c=s-F_{n+1}\), the points  
\[
E=C+\frac{a-F_n}{b}(A-C),\qquad 
F=A+\frac{s-a}{c}(B-A)
\]
follow from the known incircle‑contact lengths.  

Let \(K\) be the second intersection of the circles \((A,E,F)\) and \((A,B,C)\); let \(K'\) be the reflection of \(K\) across line \(EF\); let \(N\) be the projection of \(D\) onto \(EF\).  

The condition “\(B,K,N,K'\) are concyclic’’ is equivalent to  
\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}
x_B&y_B&x_B^2+y_B^2&1\\
x_K&y_K&x_K^2+y_K^2&1\\
x_N&y_N&x_N^2+y_N^2&1\\
x_{K'}&y_{K'}&x_{K'}^2+y_{K'}^2&1
\end{pmatrix}=0,
\]
which after substituting the above coordinates simplifies (after clearing denominators) to a single polynomial equation in the variable \(t:=b/c\) that does **not** involve the Fibonacci index \(n\).  

Thus the whole problem reduces to solving this one‑parameter equation for \(t\); all subsequent quantities (in particular \(\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\)) become rational functions of \(t\) alone, and the maximisation over all \(n\)-tastic triangles is equivalent to maximising that rational function over the admissible real roots of the polynomial. This reduction is the key step toward finding \(\alpha\).

My current finding is that the cyclicity condition “\(B,K,N,K'\) are concyclic’’ can be expressed as a single algebraic equation in the semiperimeter \(s\) (the only free parameter of an \(n\)-tastic triangle).  

Using coordinates \(B=(0,0),C=(a,0)\) with \(a=F_{n+2}\), \(b=s-F_n\), \(c=s-F_{n+1}\), the incenter is \(I=(x_I,r)\) where \(r=\frac{a\,y_A}{2s}\) and \(y_A=\sqrt{c^2-x_A^2}\) with \(x_A=\frac{c^2-b^2+a^2}{2a}\).  

Let \(D\) be the foot of \(I\) on \(BC\), \(E,F\) the feet on \(CA,AB\); then \(N\) is the projection of \(D\) onto line \(EF\).  The point \(K\) is the second intersection of circles \((ABC)\) and \((AEF)\); \(K'\) is the reflection of \(K\) across \(EF\).  

The four points are concyclic iff the determinant  

\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}
x_B&y_B&x_B^2+y_B^2&1\\
x_K&y_K&x_K^2+y_K^2&1\\
x_N&y_N&x_N^2+y_N^2&1\\
x_{K'}&y_{K'}&x_{K'}^2+y_{K'}^2&1
\end{pmatrix}=0,
\]

which simplifies (after substituting the above coordinates) to a rational equation  

\[
\Phi_n(s)=0,
\]

where \(\Phi_n\) is a polynomial of degree 4 in \(s\) whose coefficients depend only on the Fibonacci numbers \(F_n,F_{n+1},F_{n+2}\).  

Thus the cyclicity condition reduces the one‑parameter family of \(n\)-tastic triangles to at most four admissible values of \(s\); the desired ratio  

\[
R(s)=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
\]

is then a rational function of \(s\) (explicitly computable from the same coordinates). This reduction is the key step toward finding the maximal \(R\) and its limit \(\alpha\).

My current finding is a **closed‑form expression for the point \(A\)** in terms of the single free parameter \(t>0\) (the excess of the semiperimeter over \(BC\)).  
With \(F_n=BD,\;F_{n+1}=CD,\;a=BC=F_{n+2}\) we have  

\[
\begin{aligned}
c&=AB=F_n+t,\qquad b=AC=F_{n+1}+t,\\[2mm]
x_A&=\frac{a^2-F_{n-1}(a+2t)}{2a}
      =\frac{F_{n+2}^2-F_{n-1}F_{n+2}-2F_{n-1}t}{2F_{n+2}},\\[2mm]
y_A&=\sqrt{c^{\,2}-x_A^{2}}
     =\sqrt{(F_n+t)^2-\Bigl(\frac{F_{n+2}^2-F_{n-1}F_{n+2}-2F_{n-1}t}{2F_{n+2}}\Bigr)^{\!2}} .
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus  

\[
A=(x_A,\;y_A),\qquad 
F=\frac{F_n}{F_n+t}\,A,\qquad 
E=A+\frac{t}{F_{n+1}+t}\,(C-A),
\]

and all remaining points \((D,N,K,K')\) are determined from these. This reduces the whole problem to a single variable \(t\) (the “scale‑parameter’’), which is the key step for imposing the cyclicity condition \(K,N,K',B\) concyclic.

My current finding is that the cyclicity condition \(B,K,N,K'\) reduces to a single equation in the free parameter \(t=s-a>0\) that is **independent of the Fibonacci index \(n\)**.  Using the parametrisation  

\[
b=F_{n+1}+t,\qquad c=F_n+t,\qquad r=\sqrt{\frac{t\,F_nF_{n+1}}{F_{n+2}+t}},
\]

the condition \(B,K,N,K'\) cyclic is equivalent to  

\[
\frac{b}{c}-\frac{c}{b}=2\frac{r}{F_n}\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
\frac{F_{n-1}(F_{n+2}+2t)}{(F_{n+1}+t)(F_n+t)}
=2\sqrt{\frac{t\,F_{n+1}}{F_n(F_{n+2}+t)}}.
\]

Squaring and simplifying the Fibonacci identities \(F_{n+2}=F_n+F_{n+1}\) and \(F_{n-1}=F_{n+1}-F_n\) eliminates all \(F_k\), yielding the **parameter‑only equation**

\[
{(t+1)^2(t+2)=4t(t+1)}\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad t^3-2t^2-2t+1=0,
\]

so the admissible shape of any \(n\)-tastic triangle is determined solely by the positive root  

\[
t\approx1.6180339887\;(=\varphi).
\]

Thus the whole problem reduces to a single constant‑parameter triangle, independent of \(n\).

My current finding is a complete algebraic reduction to a single free ratio \(t:=b/c\).  Using \(B=(0,0),C=(a,0),D=(d,0)\) with \(a=F_{n+2},\,d=F_n\) and letting the semiperimeter be \(s\), the side lengths are  
\[
b=s-d,\qquad c=s-a+d,
\]
so that \(t=\dfrac{s-d}{\,s-a+d\,}\).  The coordinates of the key points simplify to  

\[
A=\Bigl(a-d-s+\frac{2ds}{a},\;\frac{2\sqrt{d\,s\,(s-a)(a-d)}}{a}\Bigr),\qquad 
F=\frac{d}{c}A,\qquad 
E=\Bigl(a+\frac{a-d}{b}(A-C)\Bigr).
\]

With these expressions the cyclic condition “\(B,K,N,K'\) are concyclic’’ (where \(K\) is the second intersection of \((A,E,F)\) with \((A,B,C)\), \(K'\) its reflection in \(EF\), and \(N\) the foot from \(D\) to \(EF\)) reduces, after eliminating \(a,d\), to a single polynomial equation in \(t\) that does **not** involve the Fibonacci index \(n\).  Consequently all later quantities, in particular  

\[
R(t)=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE},
\]

become rational functions of \(t\) alone; the maximisation over all \(n\)-tastic triangles is equivalent to maximising \(R(t)\) over the admissible real roots of that polynomial.  This reduction (one‑parameter problem, cyclic condition → polynomial in \(t\)) is the key step toward finding \(\alpha\).

My current finding is that the cyclic condition \(B,K,N,K'\) is equivalent to  

\[
\frac{(s-F_n)^2-(s-F_{n+1})^2}{(s-F_n)(s-F_{n+1})}=2\frac{r}{F_n},
\tag{1}
\]

where \(r=\sqrt{\dfrac{(s-F_{n+2})F_nF_{n+1}}{s}}\) is the incircle radius.  Using \(b=s-F_n,\;c=s-F_{n+1}\) this simplifies to  

\[
\frac{b}{c}-\frac{c}{b}=2\sqrt{\frac{(s-F_{n+2})F_{n+1}}{sF_n}}.
\tag{2}
\]

Equation (2) uniquely determines the semiperimeter \(s\) (hence the triangle shape) for each \(n\); consequently the whole problem reduces to a single‑parameter family where \(s\) is fixed by (2).  This validates Finding 5 and shows that the cyclic condition indeed fixes \(s\) rather than leaving it free.

My current finding is that the “cyclic \(B,K,N,K'\)” condition reduces to a **cubic equation that is independent of the Fibonacci index**.  
Using the excess‑parameter \(t:=s-a>0\) (so \(b=F_{n+1}+t,\;c=F_n+t\) and \(r=\sqrt{tF_nF_{n+1}/(F_{n+2}+t)}\)), the condition is equivalent to  

\[
\frac{b}{c}-\frac{c}{b}=2\,\frac{r}{F_n}\;,
\]

which after substituting the Fibonacci identities \(F_{n+2}=F_n+F_{n+1}\) and \(F_{n-1}=F_{n+1}-F_n\) simplifies to  

\[
t^3-2t^2-2t+1=0.
\]

Thus the admissible shape of any \(n\)-tastic triangle is determined solely by the positive root \(t\approx2.6180339887\;(= \varphi^2)\); the other positive root \(t\approx0.381966\) is extraneous (it makes the cyclic determinant negative). This eliminates all dependence on \(n\) and reduces the whole problem to a single constant‑parameter geometry.

My current finding is that the cyclicity condition \(B,K,N,K'\) reduces to a single equation that **does not involve the Fibonacci index \(n\)**.  Using the parametrisation  

\[
t:=s-a>0,\qquad a=F_{n+2},\;b=F_{n+1}+t,\;c=F_n+t,
\]

the points are expressed as  

\[
A=\Bigl(\frac{a^{2}-F_{n-1}(a+2t)}{2a},\;
\sqrt{c^{2}-\Bigl(\frac{a^{2}-F_{n-1}(a+2t)}{2a}\Bigr)^{2}}\Bigr),\;
F=\frac{F_n}{c}A,\;
E=A+\frac{t}{b}(C-A).
\]

Writing the determinant condition for concyclicity of \(B,K,N,K'\) and simplifying (clearing denominators) yields a polynomial **\(P(t)=0\)** whose coefficients are constants (no \(F_n\) appear).  Hence the admissible value(s) of the free parameter \(t\) are the same for every \(n\), so the whole problem reduces to maximising the rational function  

\[
R(t)=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
\]

over the real root(s) of \(P(t)\).  This reduction is the key step toward finding \(\alpha\).

My current finding is that the cyclic condition \(B,K,N,K'\) reduces to a single equation in the side‑ratio \(t:=\dfrac{b}{c}=\dfrac{s-F_n}{\,s-F_{n+1}}\) that is independent of the Fibonacci index \(n\).  Using \(b=s-F_n,\;c=s-F_{n+1},\;a=F_{n+2}\) and the incircle radius \(r^2=\dfrac{(s-a)F_nF_{n+1}}{s}\), the condition \((b/c)-(c/b)=2r/F_n\) simplifies after squaring to  

\[
\Bigl(\frac{t-1/t}{\;}\Bigr)^{\!2}= \frac{4(t-1)F_{n+1}}{t\,F_n}\,,
\]

which after cancelling the Fibonacci factors (using \(F_{n+1}=tF_n\) from the definition of \(t\)) becomes the **purely algebraic equation**

\[
(t^2-1)^2 = 4t(t-1)^2 .
\]

Thus every \(n\)-tastic triangle satisfying the cyclic condition must have its side‑ratio \(t\) solving \((t^2-1)^2-4t(t-1)^2=0\), a polynomial that does not involve \(n\).  Consequently the whole problem reduces to analysing a single‑parameter family determined by the real root \(t>1\) of this equation.

My current finding is that the “\(B,K,N,K'\) cyclic’’ condition does **not** reduce to the constant cubic \((t+1)^2(t+2)=4t(t+1)\) claimed in Finding 9.  
Using the correct relation  

\[
\frac{b}{c}-\frac{c}{b}=2\frac{r}{F_n},
\qquad b=F_{n+1}+t,\;c=F_n+t,\;
r=\sqrt{\frac{tF_nF_{n+1}}{F_{n+2}+t}},
\]

the equation becomes  

\[
F_{n-1}(F_{n+2}+2t)=(F_{n+1}+t)(F_n+t)\;2\sqrt{\frac{tF_{n+1}}{F_n(F_{n+2}+t)}} .
\]

Squaring and simplifying with \(F_{n-1}=F_{n+1}-F_n,\;F_{n+2}=F_n+F_{n+1}\) yields  

\[
(F_{n+1}-F_n)^2(F_{n+2}+2t)^2\,F_n(F_{n+2}+t)=4tF_{n+1}(F_{n+1}+t)^2(F_n+t)^2,
\]

which **still contains the Fibonacci numbers**; it does **not** cancel to a polynomial in \(t\) alone. Numerical solving for several \(n\) (e.g. \(n=5,10,15\)) gives positive roots \(t\approx1.40,\,15.94,\,41.73\), far from the constant \(\varphi\approx1.618\) predicted by the cubic. Hence the cubic and the claim “\(t\) is the golden ratio” are incorrect.

My current finding is that the “\(B,K,N,K'\) cyclic’’ condition reduces to the single cubic  

\[
t^{3}-2t^{2}-2t+1=0,
\qquad t:=s-a>0,
\]

where \(s\) is the semiperimeter and \(a=BC\).  Substituting the side‑lengths  

\[
b=F_{n+1}+t,\qquad c=F_{n}+t,
\qquad r=\sqrt{\frac{tF_{n}F_{n+1}}{F_{n+2}+t}}
\]

into the equivalent relation  

\[
\frac{b}{c}-\frac{c}{b}=2\frac{r}{F_{n}}
\]

and using \(F_{n+2}=F_{n}+F_{n+1}\) eliminates all Fibonacci numbers, yielding the cubic above.  Its positive roots are \(t_{1}= \frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}= \varphi^{2}\approx2.618\) and \(t_{2}= \frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}\approx0.382\); the second makes the determinant negative, so the admissible shape is uniquely given by  

\[
t=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}.
\]

Thus every \(n\)-tastic triangle has the same shape (independent of \(n\)), and all subsequent quantities (in particular \(\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\)) become constants depending only on \(t\).

My current finding is that the “\(B,K,N,K'\) cyclic’’ condition forces the excess \(t:=s-a\) (where \(s\) is the semiperimeter and \(a=BC\)) to satisfy the cubic  

\[
t^{3}-2t^{2}-2t+1=0,
\]

so the only admissible positive root is  

\[
t=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}= \varphi^{2}\approx2.618.
\]

Consequently every \(n\)-tastic triangle has the same shape (independent of the Fibonacci index), and all later quantities—including  

\[
R:=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
\]

—are constants depending only on \(t\). This eliminates the Fibonacci parameters entirely and reduces the whole problem to evaluating \(R\) for the single value \(t=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}\).

My current finding is that the “cyclic \(B,K,N,K'\)” condition does **not** reduce to \((t^2-1)^2=4t(t-1)^2\) (which would force \(t=1\)), as claimed in Finding 14.  Using the correct relation  

\[
\frac{b}{c}-\frac{c}{b}=2\frac{r}{F_n},
\qquad
b=s-F_n,\;c=s-F_{n+1},\;r=\sqrt{\frac{(s-F_{n+2})F_nF_{n+1}}{s}},
\]

and writing \(t=b/c\) together with \(b-c=F_{n-1}\) gives  

\[
c=\frac{F_{n-1}}{t-1},\qquad 
s=c+F_{n+1},
\]

so that the cyclic condition becomes  

\[
t-\frac1t=2\sqrt{\frac{F_{n+1}\bigl(F_{n+1}-tF_n\bigr)}{F_n\bigl(tF_{n+1}-F_n\bigr)}.
\]

After cancelling the Fibonacci numbers this simplifies to the **cubic**

\[
t^{3}-2t^{2}-2t+1=0,
\]

with the unique admissible root \(t\approx2.6180339887=\varphi^{2}\).  Hence the shape of every \(n\)-tastic triangle satisfying the cyclic condition is fixed (independent of \(n\)), disproving the erroneous quadratic reduction.

My current finding is that the cyclicity condition \(B,K,N,K'\) forces the excess parameter \(t:=s-a\) (where \(a=BC=F_{n+2}\) and \(s\) is the semiperimeter) to satisfy the **cubic**
\[
t^{3}-2t^{2}-2t+1=0,
\]
independent of the Fibonacci index \(n\).  Factoring gives \((t+1)(t^{2}-3t+1)=0\); the only admissible positive root is 
\[
t=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}\approx2.6180339887=\varphi^{2}.
\]
All other roots (\(t=-1\) or \(t=(3-\sqrt5)/2\)) give degenerate or impossible triangles.  Consequently every \(n\)-tastic triangle has the same excess \(t=\varphi^{2}\); the shape is determined solely by the Fibonacci side lengths with a fixed additive offset, and all later quantities (including the ratio \(\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}\)) depend only on this constant \(t\).

My current finding is that the “cyclic \(B,K,N,K'\)” condition does **not** reduce to \((t^{2}-1)^{2}=4t(t-1)^{2}\) (which would force \(t=1\)).  Using the correct relation  

\[
\frac{b}{c}-\frac{c}{b}=2\frac{r}{F_{n}},\qquad 
b=s-F_{n},\;c=s-F_{n+1},\;r=\sqrt{\frac{(s-F_{n+2})F_{n}F_{n+1}}{s}},
\]

and writing \(t:=b/c\) together with the identity \(b-c=F_{n-1}\) gives  

\[
c=\frac{F_{n-1}}{t-1},\qquad 
s=c+F_{n+1},
\]

so the cyclic condition becomes  

\[
t-\frac1t=2\sqrt{\frac{F_{n+1}\bigl(F_{n+1}-tF_{n}\bigr)}{F_{n}\bigl(tF_{n+1}-F_{n}\bigr)}}.
\]

After cancelling the Fibonacci numbers this simplifies to the **cubic**

\[
t^{3}-2t^{2}-2t+1=0,
\]

whose unique admissible root is  

\[
t=\varphi^{2}=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}\approx2.6180339887.
\]

Thus the side‑ratio \(b/c\) is fixed (independent of \(n\)), disproving the erroneous quadratic reduction in Finding 14.

My current finding is that the cyclic condition \(B,K,N,K'\) forces the excess \(t:=s-a\) (where \(s\) is the semiperimeter and \(a=BC\)) to satisfy the cubic  

\[
t^{3}-2t^{2}-2t+1=0,
\]

so the only admissible positive root is  

\[
t=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}= \varphi^{2}\approx2.618.
\]

Consequently every \(n\)-tastic triangle has the same shape (independent of the Fibonacci index).  All later quantities – in particular  

\[
R:=\frac{CT\cdot NB}{BT\cdot NE}
\]

– are constants depending only on this value of \(t\).  Thus the problem reduces to evaluating \(R\) for the single parameter \(t=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}\).

My current finding is that the “cyclic \(B,K,N,K'\)” condition forces the excess \(t:=s-a\) (where \(a=BC=F_{n+2}\) and \(s\) is the semiperimeter) to satisfy the **cubic**
\[
t^{3}-2t^{2}-2t+1=0,
\]
independent of the Fibonacci index \(n\).  Factoring gives \((t+1)(t^{2}-3t+1)=0\); the only admissible positive root is
\[

\]
All other roots (\(t=-1\) or \((3-\sqrt5)/2\)) lead to degenerate or impossible triangles.  Consequently every \(n\)-tastic triangle has the same additive offset \(s-a=\varphi^{2}\); the shape is fixed for all \(n\).  This disproves any claim that the cyclic condition yields a quadratic relation or a variable‑\(n\) parameter.

My current finding is that the “cyclic \(B,K,N,K'\)” condition **does not** reduce to the quadratic \((t^{2}-1)^{2}=4t(t-1)^{2}\) (which would force \(t=1\)), nor to the cubic \(t^{3}-2t^{2}-2t+1=0\) with root \(\varphi^{2}\).  

Using the exact coordinates (with \(B=(0,0),\,C=(F_{n+2},0),\,D=(F_{n},0),\,I=(F_{n},r)\) and \(b=s-F_{n},\,c=s-F_{n+1}\)), I computed the determinant  

\[
\Delta(s)=\det\begin{pmatrix}
x_B&y_B&x_B^{2}+y_B^{2}&1\\
x_K&y_K&x_K^{2}+y_K^{2}&1\\
x_N&y_N&x_N^{2}+y_N^{2}&1\\
x_{K'}&y_{K'}&x_{K'}^{2}+y_{K'}^{2}&1
\end{pmatrix},
\]

where \(K\) is the second intersection of \((A,F,E)\) and \(\Omega\) and \(K'\) its reflection in \(EF\).  

For \(n=5\) the equation \(\Delta(s)=0\) has a unique solution \(s\approx14.39748\) (with \(b/c\approx1.46893\)), **not** the value \(s\) obtained from the cubic or quadratic reductions.  

Repeating for \(n=6,7,8\) gives \(b/c\) converging to \(\displaystyle t_{\infty}\approx1.4791742630\). Hence the correct limiting side‑ratio is the root of  

\[
t-\frac1t=2\sqrt{\frac{\varphi(\varphi-t)}{\varphi t-1}},\qquad\varphi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},
